newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Reserves hold S.Africa stocks firm until close.
newsitem.headline: Reserves hold S.Africa stocks firm until close.

text.p: A massive 7.4 billion rand jump in South African May gold and foreign reserves data underlined a strong stock market on Tuesday, although shares tipped off their peaks towards the close on profit-taking.
Futures-related appetite for shares also aided blue-chips' gains with heavyweight financial stocks a favourite, propelling the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's financial index to a new closing high.

Dealers and analysts said local institutions, who have held to the sidelines in recent weeks amid a slew of poor company results, returned as strong buyers further encouraged by renewed talk of an interest rate cut as soon as the third quarter.
The industrial index finished up 46.4 points at 8,336.8, which together with robust gains in key index stocks Anglo and De Beers, helped the all-share index up 50.7 to 7,112.0.
On the stock market's gold board, activity was overshadowed by industrials' performance. The index dipped 8.4 to 1,158.2 as bullion slipped below the $344 level.
Stocks were seen firm for the third consecutive day on Wednesday, supported by continued institutional interest.
